author: @Copilot

evidence.api_compatibility: Breaking CLI change: --no-sign flag is removed. Operators who previously ran the release tool with --no-sign will now get an unrecognized flag error. The migration path is documented in the PR and in docs/dev/release.md — they should omit the flag (it is now the default) or use --sign if they want a signed tag. This is a release-admin tool, not an end-user API, so impact is limited but must be noted in release notes.
evidence.documentation: docs/dev/release.md was updated to reflect the new default (annotated unsigned tags) and the --sign opt-in syntax. The updated examples in the doc match the new CLI. Release process steps remain unchanged; only the tag creation detail shifted.
evidence.manual_release_testing: The release tagging tool is a user-facing CLI used by release admins to promote candidates to stable. The PR changes the default tag type from signed to annotated and removes --no-sign in favor of --sign. CI runs do not exercise the release script (it is a local release operator tool), so there is no evidence a human ran the default path end-to-end. The dry-run flags should be verified as a release-critical check before the v2026.41 tag.
evidence.post_approval_commits: No commits were added after either approval. The PR contains two commits (Initial plan by Copilot, Default release tags to unsigned by Copilot co-authored with superm1), and both approvals landed on the final commit f41046241a15daac1a6be13b52634c6e67715c51. The merge was clean with no post-approval churn.
evidence.review: Two substantive approvals from @superm1 (approved 2026-09-23T16:28:01Z) and @jeremyfowers (approved 2026-09-24T19:04:05Z), both on commit f41046241a15daac1a6be13b52634c6e67715c51. @superm1 has subject area expertise in linux packaging, security, Docker, containers, llamacpp, NPU — directly relevant to the release script. @jeremyfowers has expertise in CI and governance. No inline review comments were left. Both reviewers are maintainers.
evidence.security: No security concerns. The change reduces the default tag from signed to annotated, which is a relaxation of the prior default but is intentional — signing requires local GPG setup that many operators lack. The error message for failed signing now provides actionable guidance ("Configure git tag signing or rerun without --sign"). No credential handling, network calls, or supply-chain changes.
evidence.tests: New test test_signed_tag_failure_explains_how_to_proceed (test/test_release.py) verifies the signed-tag failure path raises a RuntimeError with the actionable message. The existing test_create_release_tags_and_pushes was updated to remove the sign=False parameter. The test suite covers both the default (unsigned) and signed-tag failure paths for the release script logic. No evidence of test weakening or deletion.

subject: Default release.py to unsigned tags (#3660)
summary: Default the release tagging tool to create unsigned annotated tags instead of signed tags, with --sign as explicit opt-in, fixing an ambiguous git error when tag signing is not configured locally.
verdict_reason: The release tool's CLI behavior changed (replacing --no-sign with --sign) but no evidence shows a human exercised the new default path end-to-end before merging.
